description.value: We investigated the relationship between duration of PTSD and grey matter volume in the hippocampus and rostral anterior cingulate, and compared grey matter volume between PTSD participants and trauma-exposed controls.

spans.text: In this study, we investigated the relationship between duration of PTSD and grey matter volume in the hippocampus and rostral anterior cingulate.

value: We predicted that the PTSD group would display reduced grey matter volume in these regions compared with trauma-exposed controls (TCs), and that these deficits would be magnified with greater duration of PTSD symptoms.

value: There were significant reductions in bilateral hippocampal volume in the PTSD compared with controls.
Significant reductions in bilateral rostral anterior cingulate volumes were also observed for the PTSD relative to controls.
The structural volume differences between PTSD and TCs in hippocampus and anterior cingulate support previous evidence of reduced right hippocampal and rostral anterior cingulate volumes in PTSD.

To investigate the relationship between duration of PTSD and hippocampal and anterior cingulate grey matter volume, regression analyses were performed at each grey matter voxel in these regions for the PTSD and control groups, respectively.
A significant negative correlation between time since trauma and right hippocampal volume was observed in the PTSD group
A significant negative correlation between time since trauma and right hippocampal volume was observed

value: A significant negative correlation between time since trauma and right hippocampal volume was observed in the PTSD group after controlling for DASS depression and PTSD severity.

This negative correlation suggests that as the duration of PTSD increases, right hippocampal volume decreases. No significant relationships were found between grey matter volume in other regions of interest and time since trauma for either group.

description.value: Voxel-based morphometry preprocessing included spatial normalization to the ICBM 152 template, reslicing, tissue segmentation, removal of extracerebral voxels, and modulation with Jacobian determinants.

spans.text: Brain images were spatially normalized by transforming each brain into a standardized stereotactic space based on the ICBM 152 template
The normalized images were resliced with 1.5×0.1.5×1.5 mm voxels, before being segmented into grey matter, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid probability maps, and stripped of extracerebral voxels.
